meaning: How much the spacecraft must change its speed to make a trip. More Δv means more fuel.
How efficient an engine is. A higher number means it needs less fuel for the same push.
The formula that links fuel, mass and Δv. Every real rocket is designed with it.
The short period when Earth and the target planet are in the right positions, so the spacecraft can get there with a normal amount of fuel.
The curved path around the Sun that a spacecraft follows from one planet to another.
The cheapest transfer orbit between two circular orbits. It is half an ellipse.
Astronomical Unit: the distance from Earth to the Sun, about 150 million km.
A power source that makes electricity from heat. It works just as well far from the Sun.
The braking burn that slows the spacecraft enough to be captured. Too little fuel and it flies straight past.
When a spacecraft notices something wrong it shuts almost everything down and waits for instructions.
NASA's giant radio dishes in California, Spain and Australia. Every deep-space mission shares them.
Our made-up score for what each instrument is worth, so missions can be compared. Real science is not a number.
After you arrive, the planets carry on round their orbits and your spacecraft rides round the one it reached. Nothing in space stops.
